sources.summary: On Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury announced new sanctions on a Panama-based law firm and five of its staff for allegedly helping Iranian shipping intere...
sources.text: U.S. Treasury Sanctions Shipping Law Firm for Alleged Shadow Fleet Services The bulker Gloris, seen here under a previous name in 2023, allegedly moved Iranian goods after her owning company was registered by Karnakis and Karnakis (VesselFinder / Tony Roberts file image) By The Maritime Executive 2026-10-21 22:52:06 On Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury announced new sanctions on a Panama-based law firm and five of its staff for allegedly helping Iranian shipping interests. The action is intended to send a message to maritime service providers and further tighten the American net around Iranian international commerce. According to the Treasury, Karnakis and Karnakis was particularly active in its work on behalf of the Seyed Asadoollah Emamjomeh shipping network, which specialized in Iranian LPG exports. Emamjomeh's network was sanctioned last year; Treasury is effectively working its way upstream to target people who provided it with professional services. The department alleges that Karnakis and Karnakis helped clients to register corporate entities that own shadow fleet vessels in Iranian trades, thereby enabling the transport of Iranian petrochemicals, petroleum, steel and other commodities. Examples allegedly include the sanctioned shipping companies Skyros Maritime and Trading SA, Corfu Maritime and Trading SA, and Elias Shipping and Trading Group SA. Elias is the owner of the Ramona 1, a sanctioned tanker linked to oil sales on behalf of Yemen's Houthi rebels and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. “Whether you are conducting illegal oil transfers at sea or sitting in the corner office of a law firm, if you are supporting the Iranian regime, we will find you and sanction you,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent in a statement. “We know who you are, we know what you’re doing, and we will continue to take action.” Stay on Top of the Daily Maritime News The maritime news that matters most Get the latest maritime news delivered to your inbox daily. Subscribe Free Treasury also personally sanctioned the law firm's founders, along with three employees who had allegedly served as listed directors and officers of the holding companies that Karnakis and Karnakis created. Also sanctioned were shipping agency Amigoz Singapore, accused of providing bunkering and services for shadow fleet entities; and Whales Shipping Line, based in the UAE, for alleged involvement with Iranian petrochemical trading.

sources.title: French Navy Reports Drone Incursion During Harbor-Protection Exercises
sources.summary: On Wednesday, the French navy issued an alert reporting an unlawful drone incursion - this time, during a military exercise. According to the Marine N...
sources.text: French Navy Reports Drone Incursion During Harbor-Protection Exercises The Toulon naval harbor, 2009 (Jesfr / CC BY SA 3.0) By The Maritime Executive 2026-10-21 21:43:28 On Wednesday, the French navy issued an alert reporting an unlawful drone incursion - this time, during a military exercise. According to the Marine Nationale, several unauthorized drone flights were detected in restricted airspace during a series of exercises near Toulon. "To date, no sensitive infrastructure has been threatened. A judicial investigation has been opened," the Marine Nationale said. "For each incident, the planned security measures were activated by triggering anti-drone systems, coordinated with the internal security forces." French radio station Ici Provence, which first reported the incursions, said that the overflights occurred over Toulon's naval base - the largest naval station in Western Europe - along with the directorate of armaments building in Toulon and the base of the 54th Artillery Regiment in Hyeres. The source reported that the drones were "large machines," but the specific type and number were unknown. Electromagnetic jamming systems were used to counteract the incursion. The drones arrived during a joint French military exercise focused on the defense of harborside installations in Toulon, with military units working alongside internal security forces. Air traffic near the exercise was prohibited to allow for unencumbered military operations - including authorized drone operations. Stay on Top of the Daily Maritime News The maritime news that matters most Get the latest maritime news delivered to your inbox daily. Subscribe Free The Marine Nationale's report is the latest in a series of escalating drone disruptions, some attributed to Russian interference. The most dramatic example occurred in early August at Leipzig Airport, when drones armed with military-grade explosives approached Ukrainian transport aircraft on the tarmac. The attack was narrowly averted; German intelligence has identified the Russian sabotage unit likely responsible for the Leipzig incident as GRU Unit 29155, and specifically a team of agents led by Russian-Latvian dual national Oleg Levushkin. Top image: Toulon naval harbor, 2009 ( Jesfr / CC BY SA 3.0 )

sources.title: Iraqi Line Resumes Shipping After 50 Year Hiatus
sources.summary: An Iraqi-owned container ship departed the port of Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates today, October 21, northbound in the Persian Gulf. What makes...
sources.text: Iraqi Line Resumes Shipping After 50 Year Hiatus The Iraqi cargo ship Basrah will start a commercial shuttle service in the Persian Gulf (Ministry of Transport) By The Maritime Executive 2026-10-21 15:44:57 An Iraqi-owned container ship departed the port of Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates today, October 21, northbound in the Persian Gulf. What makes the departure so notable is that it signals Iraq’s efforts to revive a state-owned shipping line after a more than 50-year hiatus. The country’s Ministry of Transport had announced at the beginning of the month the plan to restore a national shipping line. It cited the opportunities to increase the flow of goods in the Persian Gulf, along with supporting trade with the country’s neighbors. The report said the new initiative aligns with the strategic objectives to develop the country’s transport infrastructure and enhance its operational capabilities. While the initial reports had said the service would launch in mid-month, it may have been delayed by the recent escalations by Iran. In a report put out by UK Maritime Trade Operations on October 21, it said it had been informed by a master that a tanker had been struck by an unknown projectile. It called it a late report and said the incident had happened 30 nautical miles southeast of Al Faw, Iraq. Iraqi officials have not confirmed the details. Experts note that most cargo has been flowing overland since the start of the war. Ports in the UAE, Oman, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan, outside the Gulf, have reported increases in cargo volumes as shippers sought alternatives to move cargo in the region, but the road and rail networks are lacking and believed to be strained. Iraq has owned the cargo ship Basrah since it was built in 2014. The vessel is 17,787 dwt and measures 143 meters (469 feet) in length. Alphaliner reports it was outfitted to carry approximately 900 TEU. It is registered in Jordan. The vessel’s AIS signal shows its departure from Jebel Ali Port today. It is reporting a destination of Kuwait, with the Ministry reporting the shuttle service would also connect to Iraq’s southern port of Umm Qasr. Stay on Top of the Daily Maritime News The maritime news that matters most Get the latest maritime news delivered to your inbox daily. Subscribe Free In April, the Ministry reported the vessel was being used to address strains on the supply chain and specifically food supplies since the start of the war in the region. Media reports highlighted the ship’s arrival at Umm Qasr loaded with a shipment of foodstuffs. The Ministry highlighted that the last commercial voyages conducted by Iraqi cargo vessels in the region dated back to the mid-1690s. It called the resumption of the services a significant milestone in the efforts to reactivate national carriers and advance Iraq’s maritime transport sector.

sources.title: The Defensive Alliance to Deter Chinese Maritime Expansion is Strengthening
sources.summary: An overview of a series of separate developments suggests that a string of Asian nations facing pressure from China across maritime borders are cooper...
sources.text: The Defensive Alliance to Deter Chinese Maritime Expansion is Strengthening USS Theodore Roosevelt docks in Yokosuka, October 16 (US Navy) By The Maritime Executive 2026-10-21 14:22:33 An overview of a series of separate developments suggests that a string of Asian nations facing pressure from China across maritime borders are cooperating more fully as a means of countering the threat. Exercise Keen Sword has commenced and is running until October 29. The exercise principally involves 45,000 Japanese and 12,000 US troops. But the exercise also involves seven other Asian and European nations, with participation for the first time in this recurring exercise by France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and the Philippines. South Korea is participating as an observer, having trained with Japan and the United States on Exercise Freedom Edge last month. Keen Sword is focused on two geographical areas: Japan’s southwestern islands, where there is competition with China, and the Kuril Islands, ownership of which is disputed with Russia. With Japan-based carrier USS George Washington otherwise engaged in the Central Command area, the USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71), the Ticonderoga Class guided-missile cruiser USS Chosin (CG 65) and the Arleigh Burke Class destroyer USS Decatur (DDG 73) have arrived at the US naval base in Yokusuka to join in the exercise. USS Theodore Roosevelt is the first non-forward-deployed carrier in four years to dock in Yokosuka. During the exercise, Japanese forces and US Marines will deploy (respectively) Type-25 land-to-ship missiles and the NMESIS ground-based missile system on the island of Yonaguni. With ranges of over 500 nautical miles, these missiles can reach large swathes of the Chinese mainland coastline, as well as the eastern and southern flanks of Taiwan. Japanese ownership of Yonaguni is disputed by China, which frequently intrudes into Japanese territorial waters around the island, and the island is also claimed by Taiwan. However, Taiwanese Defense Minister Wellington Koo has praised the Japanese and American exercise deployments on Yonaguni, regarding it not as an infringement of claimed sovereignty, but as support for Taiwan’s own defense. Stay on Top of the Daily Maritime News The maritime news that matters most Get the latest maritime news delivered to your inbox daily. Subscribe Free The Philippines is also deepening its ties with Taiwan, despite competing claims over certain islands in the South China Sea. Manila and Taipei have elected to make common cause against the claims made to these same islands by China. Taiwan’s Coast Guard Administration is planning for a training ship with cadets aboard to make a port call in the Philippines in October next year, the first such visit since 1974. What the Taiwanese call Dunmu or Friendship Cruises normally consist of three vessels, and the cruise to the Philippines is likely to be led by the fast combat support ship Panshi (AOE-532). Taiwan is also intending to copy the Philippines’ "assertive transparency" strategy—publicly documenting and exposing the Chinese bullying tactics employed both in the South China Sea and the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan and the Philippines have a common sea border running through the Bashi Channel, and the two nations are intending to improve joint surveillance in the area, particularly since the Chinese have stepped up circumnavigations of Taiwan.

sources.summary: After the strikes on commercial vessels off the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania, NATO has agreed to provide additional support to the region. The North...
sources.text: NATO to Support Increased Black Sea Surveillance NATO will provide additional resources to increase surveillance in the Black Sea (NATO) By The Maritime Executive 2026-10-21 13:15:44 After the strikes on commercial vessels off the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania, NATO has agreed to provide additional support to the region. The North Atlantic Council agreed on Tuesday, October 20, to the increased deployment after urging by Bulgarian and Romanian officials. NATO Allies had discussed the increase in Russia’s hybrid activities during a meeting in Bucharest, Romania, on October 15 and 16. According to the official reports, concerns had been raised about the increase in activity and the danger from hybrid activities, including sabotage, drone incidents, and cyber attacks. Romania reports that it has recorded 35 unauthorized drone incursions this year, compared to nine for all of 2025. Romanian officials said they had downed six of the drones, including two in recent days. Romania’s Defense Minister Radu Miruta said they were likely Russia’s latest-generation drones, noting they had been flying at speeds similar to jets. They were flying at approximately 280 mph, which the minister said indicated they were likely the Russian-made Geran-4 drones. “The situation remains serious, as commercial ships have been attacked and sunk close to the shores of Romania and Bulgaria, and seafarers have been killed, injured, or are still missing,” said the President of Romania, Nicusor Dan. “These attacks are unacceptable and must stop.” Both Romania and Bulgaria have declined to speculate on the source of the attacks on seven commercial vessels in the past days, which killed at least 23 seafarers and sank several of the vessels. Bulgaria, however, reports it has been successful in finding fragments from one of the drone attacks, and it is analyzing the chemical residues. NATO officials said they would also provide intelligence agents and teams to conduct forensic analysis of the explosives. Bulgarian officials said several drone systems had already been put in place to increase the monitoring in the Black Sea. They also reported that U.S. Poseidon surveillance planes had already started patrols to provide increased early warning. Stay on Top of the Daily Maritime News The maritime news that matters most Get the latest maritime news delivered to your inbox daily. Subscribe Free “NATO has already strengthened our posture along the eastern flank, including with counter-drone capabilities,” said a spokesperson for the treaty organization. Under the new agreement, NATO will be sending additional assets, including for surveillance, reconnaissance, and forensics. Reports indicate it will include maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems, and drones.

sources.title: Australian Government Seizes Historic Ship and Orders Immediate Disposal
sources.summary: The Government of New South Wales and preservationists are battling over the fate of a historic little vessel, MV Cape Don, with the local government...
sources.text: Australian Government Seizes Historic Ship and Orders Immediate Disposal Cape Don in a 2014 photo as a museum ship (Saberwyn - CC BY-SA 4.0) By The Maritime Executive 2026-10-20 18:13:50 The Government of New South Wales and preservationists are battling over the fate of a historic little vessel, MV Cape Don , with the local government announcing on October 18 it had seized the vessel for immediate disposal. Local officials are calling their actions “the last resort,” as they contend the vessel’s condition continues to worsen, posing substantial risks to public safety and the environment. NSW Maritime asserts it has been monitoring the condition of the vessel as it has further deteriorated for the past several years. It highlights that the vessel has been issued two unsafe vessel notices, and they assert they met with the owners, a private foundation, nearly 50 times, raising concerns about the vessel’s condition and the immediate need for repairs to stabilize the vessel. “I want to make it clear that NSW Maritime has been working in good faith with the owners of the MV Cape Don for many years to help restore the vessel, but its condition has only worsened, and the likelihood of the owners being able to restore it back to its former glory has become untenable,” asserted NSW Minister for Roads, Jenny Aitchison. The government swooped in on Sunday, October 18, with media reports that the police searched the vessel to ensure there was no one aboard. They declared it had been seized for immediate disposal. Cape Don in her heyday - the foundation asserts she is a special piece of Australian history (Sea Heritage Foundation) The 2,100 gross ton vessel, which is 74 meters (244 feet) in length, was built in 1962 in Newcastle by the State Dockyard. It was purpose-built for the Commonwealth Lighthouse Service in order to build, supply, and maintain lighthouses and navigation aids around Australia. She, along with two sisterships, Cape Moreton and Cape Pillar , was also called on for other duties such as surveying and recovery work. Cape Don was involved in many high-profile scientific expeditions, including the salvage of two anchors from HMS Investigator , a Royal Navy sloop that between 1801 and 1803 became the first ship to circumnavigate Australia. She was decommissioned from the Commonwealth Lighthouse Service in 1990 and sold to private operators who used her for passenger and cargo transport in the Solomon Islands and South Pacific for around a decade. Today, she is owned by the non-profit Sea Heritage Foundation and has been docked for more than 20 years in the Balls Head area in Sydney harbor. The charity argues she is one of the last surviving examples of a non-military vessel of the era, and she has been used for tours and education. In addition to being Australia’s only remaining lighthouse service tender, she is listed in the country’s register of historic vessels. The state asserts it has documented severe corrosion along the waterline, increasing the risk the vessel will take on water and cause a pollution event. They have issued orders for in situ repairs and the ultimate dry docking of the vessel, which they say the foundation has failed to undertake. They asserted the ship has not had major repairs for more than two decades and the underwater condition is unknown. NSW Maritime said the vessel “poses an unacceptable risk.” They assert that if the vessel begins to sink or capsize, potential salvage costs would be A$15 million (US$10.5 million). NSW Maritime asserts the ship is an unacceptable risk in its current condition (NSW Government) Representatives of the Sea Foundation and others are expressing outrage at the actions and saying they will fight the decision. They assert the statements coming from NSW are “blatant untruths.” They are demanding that Minister Aitchison commission an independent review of the vessel before any irreversible decision is made about her future. “The right and responsible sequence is to conduct an unbiased, independent review first and make a decision second. Reversing that order risks losing a 63-year-old piece of Australian maritime history on the strength of an assumption. Independent inspection and transparency about costs are the basis of a sound decision,” said Dr. CJ Manjarres-Wahlberg, Chairman and Director of the Sea Heritage Foundation. Sea Heritage's position is that the underwater hull is sound. They assert the ship has had three underwater inspections and several above-water surveys. Specialist contractors, they assert, have carried out hull repairs, installed automatic pumping with 24/7 alarms and cameras, and removed fuel oil from the vessel. The foundation admits the vessel needs permanent repairs in dry dock. To that end, they said dry docking planning for the Cape Don has been ongoing since December 2020. An independent assessment commissioned in August concluded that she could be towed to Garden Island for dry-docking, subject to final approvals. The timing of that docking rests with the Australian Defence Force’s scheduling at Captain Cook Dock, said the foundation. They are also demanding the NSW Transport publish the basis of its A$15 million figure so the public can compare the cost of disposal with the cost of preservation.
